newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures get boost ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures get boost ahead of holiday.

text.p: German Bunds and futures recovered in late trade on Wednesday to post gains ahead of a long holiday weekend but traders said concerns about the future of European monetary union still weighed on the market.
DTB June Bund futures ended up nine basis points at 100.90 points in heavy volumes and well off the session low at 100.43 reached in afternoon trade marked by conerns about EMU.
The late gains were tied mainly to traders buying contracts to cover short positions ahead of Thursday's regional holiday when debt trading in Germany will be closed.
Regular trading in Frankfurt resumes on Friday.

Dealers expect the market to remain jittery on Friday ahead of Sunday's run-off election in France and as the market responds to a Bundesbank statement to be issued on Wednesday after the market close on Bonn's plan to revalue gold reserves.

Some traders, however, said the French election was a more important issue for the market amid concerns the left-wing will win the run-off election and could change the market outlook on the near-term future for EMU, slated to begin in January 1999.
"I don't have concerns that foreign investors will look at the gold reserve changes as being a trick," said one trader.
